source_title: Given 5% chance of walking again, Irish man takes on 3,000-mile US trek
source_excerpt: Fergus Farrell, an Irish man who suffered a devastating spinal injury, is undertaking a 3,000-mile walk across the United States to raise awareness and funds for people living with spinal cord injuries. His journey follows a life-changing accident that left his ability to walk uncertain, with doctors giving him only a 5% chance of walking again. By taking on the demanding challenge, Farrell hopes to turn his own recovery into something that can help others facing similar difficulties, while highlighting the importance of rehabilitation, support and determination.Fergus Farrell walking 3,000 miles across the US after his spinal injuryFarrellâs walk across America is rooted in his experience of recovering from a serious spinal injury and learning to walk again. For Farrell, the prospect of walking again was particularly daunting after doctors reportedly gave him just a 5% chance of regaining that ability.That prediction placed his recovery in an uncertain position. Walking, something many people take for granted, became a goal that could not be guaranteed. His eventual ability to undertake a long-distance walking challenge represents a significant personal milestone against that background.Ireland's official government website presents Farrell's cross-country journey as an example of resilience following a serious injury. The former rugby player sustained his spinal cord injury in 2018 after an accident in the gym. His recovery required months of rehabilitation, sustained effort and a willingness to keep working towards improvements that could not be taken for granted.Farrell eventually regained enough mobility to take on challenges that once would have seemed out of reach. His first major milestone came after leaving the National Rehabilitation Hospital in Dublin. It also established a pattern that would shape his later adventures, with each challenge building on the progress he had already made.What makes the cross-country challenge so demandingFarrellâs route stretches from the Brooklyn Bridge in New York to Santa Monica Pier in California, covering approximately 4,500 kilometres, or 3,000 miles.
